tool.name: SKESA
tool.description: de novo assembly of microbial Illumina reads
tool.command:
## SKESA's own default is 32 GB. It keeps about 2 GB of whatever it is given for itself, ## so fail clearly on small allocations rather than hand it more than the job really has. MEMORY_GB=\$(( \${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-32768} / 1024 )) && if [ "\$MEMORY_GB" -lt 4 ]; then echo "SKESA needs at least 4 GB of memory but this job was given \${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB} MB; ask your Galaxy administrator to allocate more." >&2; exit 1; fi &&
skesa #if $input.type == 'single' --reads '$input.reads' #elif $input.type == 'paired' --reads '$input.forward','$input.reverse' #elif $input.type == 'paired_collection' --reads '$input.paired.forward','$input.paired.reverse' #else --reads '$input.reads' --use_paired_ends #end if #if $input.type != 'single' and $input.insert_size --insert_size $input.insert_size #end if --kmer $kmer #if $min_count --min_count $min_count #end if --min_contig $min_contig --vector_percent $vector_percent $allow_snps --cores \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} --memory \$MEMORY_GB --contigs_out '$contigs' #if $extra_outputs #if 'hist' in $extra_outputs --hist '$hist' #end if #if 'all' in $extra_outputs --all '$all_iterations' #end if #if 'connected_reads' in $extra_outputs and $input.type != 'single' --connected_reads '$connected_reads' #end if #end if

param.name: paired
param.label: Paired reads
param.help: Run on a list:paired collection to assemble each sample separately

param.name: reads
param.label: Interleaved paired reads
param.help: Mates must alternate: read 1 of a pair directly followed by read 2 (--use_paired_ends)

param.label: Minimal k-mer length
param.help: Odd number from 21 to 511. SKESA starts at this k-mer length and steps up to a maximum it estimates from the reads

validator.message: SKESA needs an odd k-mer length

param.label: Minimal k-mer count
param.help: K-mers seen fewer times are dropped when comparing alternative extensions. Leave empty to let SKESA estimate it from coverage

param.label: Vector percent
param.help: Fraction (0 to 1, above 0) of reads a 19-mer must appear in to be treated as vector/adapter and clipped before assembly. 1 disables this

validator.message: Must be above 0 and at most 1

param.label: Allow SNPs
param.help: Run an extra step that joins contigs broken by SNPs. Useful when the sample is not clonal

param.name: extra_outputs
param.label: Additional outputs
param.option: Connected paired reads (--connected_reads, paired input only)

data.name: connected_reads
data.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: connected paired reads
data.filter: extra_outputs and 'connected_reads' in extra_outputs and input['type'] != 'single'

has_text.text: Was not able to assemble anything

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
SKESA (Strategic K-mer Extension for Scrupulous Assemblies) is NCBI's de novo assembler for microbial genomes sequenced with Illumina. It extends contigs one k-mer at a time over a series of increasing k-mer lengths and stops at repeats or ambiguous branches instead of guessing, so it trades some contiguity for very few misassemblies. It is fast enough to assemble a typical bacterial genome in minutes.
-----
**Input**
Reads in FASTQ format, plain or gzipped. Choose how they are organised:
- **Paired-end: two datasets** -- forward and reverse reads in separate files. - **Paired-end: paired collection** -- one forward/reverse pair. Running the tool over a ``list:paired`` collection produces one assembly per sample. - **Paired-end: interleaved dataset** -- one file where each read 1 is followed directly by its mate. - **Single-end** -- unpaired reads.
For paired input SKESA estimates the insert size itself unless you give one.
**Options**
- **Minimal k-mer length** -- the first k-mer length used; SKESA requires an odd number of at least 21. It then steps up to a maximum estimated from read length and coverage. - **Minimal k-mer count** -- k-mers seen fewer times are ignored when SKESA chooses between alternative extensions. When left empty it is estimated from coverage. - **Minimal contig length** -- shorter contigs are not reported. - **Vector percent** -- 19-mers present in at least this fraction of reads are treated as adapter or vector and clipped. Set to 1 to disable. - **Allow SNPs** -- an extra pass that joins contigs broken by SNPs, for samples that are not clonal.
The job's cores and memory come from the Galaxy job configuration. The job fails straight away if it is given less than 4 GB, so Galaxy admins should allocate at least that (a bacterial genome typically needs 8-16 GB).
-----
**Output**
- **Contigs** (always) in FASTA. Contig names look like ``Contig_1_19.98``, where the last number is the average k-mer coverage. - **K-mer histogram** (optional): k-mer length, count, and number of k-mers with that count. - **Contigs per iteration** (optional): the contigs after each k-mer length, mostly useful for troubleshooting. - **Connected paired reads** (optional, any of the paired-end input types): read pairs SKESA merged into a single sequence spanning the insert.
**When nothing is assembled**
If SKESA assembles contigs but none reaches the minimal contig length, the job succeeds and the contigs dataset is empty, so a run over many samples is not interrupted by one poor sample. If the reads cannot be assembled at all (for example far too few reads), SKESA reports "Was not able to assemble anything" and the job fails.
